_readme: SAIRNdental licensing/credentialing rule seed. OHIO ONLY, plus the two
federal DEA rules that apply in every state.
EVERY FIGURE HERE WAS READ FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE -- the Ohio Revised Code
and the Code of Federal Regulations themselves, not from a CE vendor's
summary page. Each rule carries the citation, the URL, the verbatim quote,
and the date it was read. Same standard as sairncare_compliance_seed.json.
OHIO IS THE ONLY STATE SEEDED. api/_lib/dental-credentials.js fails closed
with NO_RULE_FOR_STATE for anything else, naming the state. A practice
licensed in a second state must have that state researched and seeded to the
same standard before this app says anything about its requirements.
Secondary sources disagree, in both directions, about when an Ohio dental
licence renews: one states 'December 31 of odd-numbered years', another
states even-numbered years. Neither matches the statute. ORC 4715.24(A)
says a licence 'expires on the date that is two years from the date of
issuance' -- a PER-LICENSEE ANNIVERSARY, not a statewide calendar date.
So there is no renewal-date rule in this file, and no code anywhere in this
feature derives an expiry from a state. Every expiration is entered from the
practice's own licence document. Encoding either calendar claim would have
produced confident wrong dates for every provider.
── WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED ─────────────────────────────────────
See unverified_notes below. Nothing there is encoded as a rule; each is
recorded as an open question rather than guessed at.

data.label: Ohio — dentists: 30 hours of continuing dental education, biennially
notes: The statute states the hours and the biennial period. It does NOT fix a calendar date for the cycle; the cycle is tied to the licensee's own registration period (see ORC 4715.24(A)), which is why each provider's cycle_start/cycle_end is entered per provider rather than computed here.

Record retention: OAC 4715-8-04 requires an applicant to keep documentation of CE taken for at least four years after the activity. This app stores the hours; it is not a substitute for keeping the certificates.

authority.quote: Each licensed dentist shall complete biennially not less than thirty hours of continuing dental education

data.label: Ohio — dental hygienists: 20 hours of continuing dental hygiene education per two-year period
notes: Twenty, not thirty. The dentist figure and the hygienist figure are different statutes and different numbers; the engine refuses to substitute one for the other (NO_RULE_FOR_ROLE) rather than defaulting.
The statute measures the hours over 'the two-year period preceding the registration period for which renewal is sought' -- i.e. the hours are earned BEFORE the period being renewed into.

authority.quote: in the two-year period preceding the registration period for which renewal is sought the registrant completed a minimum of twenty hours of continuing dental hygiene education

data.label: Ohio — a licence runs two years from ITS OWN issuance date, not a statewide calendar date
notes: This rule exists to record that expiry is NOT derivable from the state. It carries no date to compute from, deliberately.
Two widely-published secondary claims ('December 31 of odd-numbered years' and 'of even-numbered years') contradict each other and the statute. Neither is encoded.

authority.quote: A license expires on the date that is two years from the date of issuance and may be registered for additional two-year periods

data.label: Ohio — dental hygienists must hold current basic life-support certification at each renewal
accepted_issuers: American Safety and Health Institute (if determined equivalent by the board)
notes: Scoped to HYGIENISTS as the statute reads. Whether Ohio imposes the same standing requirement on dentists was NOT confirmed in this pass -- see unverified_notes. Do not extend this rule to dentists by inference.
The certification itself carries its own expiry from its issuer; that date is entered per provider as a 'certification' record.

authority.quote: shall ... be currently certified to perform basic life-support procedures by having successfully completed a basic life-support training course certified by the American red cross, the American heart association, or, if determined equivalent by the board, the American safety and health institute

data.label: DEA practitioner registration runs 36 months; renewal may be filed no earlier than 60 days before expiry
notes: The 60-day figure is the source of this feature's DEA-specific alert threshold. It is the first day a renewal can actually be FILED, so warning earlier would prompt an action the government will not yet accept.
Federal, so it applies regardless of which state the practice is licensed in -- this is the one rule here that is not Ohio-specific.

authority.quote: the registration shall expire 36 months from the initial expiration date … Any person who is registered may apply to be reregistered not more than 60 days before the expiration date of his/her registration

data.label: MATE Act — 8 hours of training on opioid/substance use disorder, one-time attestation
notes: A ONE-TIME attestation, not a recurring or expiring requirement. It is tracked as a boolean plus the date attested, alongside the DEA registration, and never as an expiry row -- showing it as 'expiring' would be wrong.
Applies to all DEA-registered practitioners except those who are solely veterinarians, which includes every DEA-registered dentist.
Attestation is made by checking a box on the online DEA registration form at the next submission, initial or renewal. This app records that it was done; it does not make the attestation.

authority.citation: Consolidated Appropriations Act 2023 §1263(a) (MATE Act), per DEA Diversion Control MATE Act FAQ
authority.quote: at least 8 hours of training … a one-time attestation … All DEA-registered practitioners, with the exception of practitioners that are solely veterinarians

verification_passes.scope: Ohio CE (dentist + hygienist), Ohio licence term, Ohio hygienist BLS, federal DEA term/renewal window, federal MATE Act.
verification_passes.method: Primary sources read directly: codes.ohio.gov for each ORC section, law.cornell.edu for 21 CFR 1301.13, DEA Diversion Control's own MATE Act FAQ. Search-engine summaries were used only to LOCATE the sources, never as the figure.
corrections: Renewal timing: secondary sources claimed a fixed statewide calendar date (and disagreed on odd vs even years). ORC 4715.24(A) says two years from issuance. No calendar date encoded.

unverified_notes: Whether Ohio requires DENTISTS (not only hygienists) to hold current BLS certification at renewal. ORC 4715.251 reads as hygienist-scoped. Parked rather than extended by inference; a dentist BLS record can still be tracked as a 'certification', it simply is not asserted here as a statutory requirement.

Ohio's specific CE subject-matter mandates, if any (e.g. required hours in particular topics). OAC 4715-8-01 sets MAXIMUM hours creditable for certain categories; the minimum-by-subject question was not researched in this pass.
The Ohio State Dental Board's own published renewal cycle page returned 404 during this pass, so the board's administrative restatement of the statute was not read. The statute itself was.
Every state other than Ohio. Nothing is claimed for any of them.
